item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"AMLO campaigned on pacification through addressing social causes, employment, welfare, reconciliation, and rejecting a frontal war approach, but his 2018-2024 plan confirmed creation of a 266-coordination Guardia Nacional built from military and federal police elements; the expectation of withdrawing the armed forces from the streets soon disappeared.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.2","2B.3","3B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The fact concerns AMLO's stated program and its institutional translation during 2018-2023.","ruler_attribution":"The document attributes the campaign promises, plan, and strategic shift directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source is an evaluative secondary report and does not independently establish all causal claims."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":11,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"Although the formal agenda invoked prevention, human rights, peacebuilding, reintegration, and institutional strengthening, the report finds that implementation centered on militarization. By 2023 the Guardia Nacional was practically composed of military personnel; 77.8% were assigned to Sedena, 10.2% to Semar, and 10.2% to the GN. AMLO promoted legal, budgetary, and administrative expansion of military security roles, and the 2022 transfer of GN control to Sedena was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in 2023.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.4","2B.8","2B.9","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","4B.4","4B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The reported institutional and legal developments include 2023 and describe the trajectory during AMLO's administration.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the expansion and perpetuation of militarization to AMLO's administration.","limitations":["The Supreme Court finding is reported by the source; the supplied text does not provide the case citation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"AMLO deployed broad unconditional cash-transfer programs to address social causes of violence, but the report finds that the programs lacked public criminogenic diagnoses, beneficiary-selection criteria tied to criminal environments, evidence-based justification, and indicators for reducing crime risk. The report says this left open the possibility that the programs served as political clientelism. His “hugs, not bullets” approach avoided targeting top cartel leaders and was accompanied by the release of Ovidio Guzmán, cordiality toward El Chapo's mother, and a statement celebrating organized crime's behavior in the 2021 elections; the policy nonetheless ended with high violence, disappearances, extortion, and political-criminal violence.","question_ids":["2B.3","2B.6","2B.9","3B.3","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","4B.2","4B.3","5B.1","5B.5","6B.1","6B.5","6B.7","7B.1","7B.8","7B.9","8B.1","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The programs and security approach operated during the AMLO period; the cited election statement concerns 2021 and the outcome assessment covers through 2023/2024.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the programs, security posture, and public statements to AMLO.","limitations":["The client request targets 2023; some cited conduct and outcome evidence extends into 2024."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":17,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"During the 2019 Culiacán operation to arrest Ovidio Guzmán for extradition, approximately 350 Army and GN personnel were overmatched by cartel forces controlling the city. To avoid further civilian and military casualties, López Obrador ordered the target released. The operation caused eight deaths and exposed intelligence, extraction-planning, coordination, and territorial-control weaknesses.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.3","2B.4","2B.7","2B.9","3B.6","3B.9","8B.5","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The crisis occurred in 2019 and is relevant as an institutional precedent for evaluating AMLO's 2023 posture.","ruler_attribution":"The decision to release the target is attributed directly to López Obrador.","limitations":["The source presents the casualty and operational account through cited press sources; the supplied units do not resolve all contested details."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":20,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"In February 2023 in Nuevo Laredo, soldiers shot at a vehicle carrying seven unarmed young people, killing five and seriously injuring one; the survivor alleged executions. In May 2023, soldiers allegedly arranged and filmed a simulated confrontation before shooting five wounded, disarmed civilians, all of whom died. The report says the cases revealed broad military discretion, possible recurrent extrajudicial execution practices, scene manipulation, and serious accountability and human-rights risks.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Both incidents occurred in 2023 and directly fit the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct is attributed to Army personnel operating under the security system expanded and maintained during AMLO's administration; direct presidential orders are not established in the supplied units.","limitations":["The report describes allegations and investigations; it does not establish personal presidential authorization."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":22,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"The report states that AMLO promised justice for Ayotzinapa but ended his administration with only three identified remains and no full resolution. It alleges that he repeatedly revictimized families, defended the Army, impeded participation by the UN and Inter-American Commission, sought to force out independent experts, and used the federal prosecutor's office to obstruct arrest warrants against military personnel. It also alleges limited resources for forced-disappearance searches, manipulation of the missing-person registry, and attacks on searching mothers.","question_ids":["2B.6","2B.9","3B.1","3B.3","3B.4","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The conduct and institutional record span AMLO's term and remained unresolved by the end of the period discussed.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the statements, institutional decisions, and alleged obstruction to López Obrador and his administration.","limitations":["Several conclusions are the report's interpretation of cited investigations and public statements."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":24,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"From 2019 to 2023, military security institutions received 72.2% of total security-institution spending; military spending rose 41.9% from 2018 while civil spending fell 50.8%. Federal transfers to states and municipalities for security programs fell 36.4%, and local security personnel fell 34% from 2018 to 2023. The GN grew to 126,203 personnel by 2023, but 94% were military and only 69% held the required police certificate.","question_ids":["2B.8","3B.2","3B.6","4B.4","5B.1","5B.6","6B.4","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The figures explicitly include 2023 and compare the inherited 2018 baseline.","ruler_attribution":"The budgetary and staffing choices are attributed to AMLO's administration.","limitations":["The figures cover the security sector and do not isolate every presidential spending decision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":29,"end_unit":30,"fact_summary":"From 2020 to 2023, local institutions performed 99.2% of presentations to prosecutors and 98.5% of emergency calls, while the GN performed 0.8% and 1.5%, respectively. GN presentations to prosecutors fell 71.4% from 2019 to 2023, while GN armed confrontations rose 904.8% and narcotics seizures fell 67.6%. The report therefore finds that the GN's material expansion did not translate into a proportionate preventive or justice contribution.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.8","3B.2","3B.6","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The performance series explicitly ends in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The institutional performance is evaluated as the result of AMLO-era policy and resource choices.","limitations":["Activity counts are proxies for performance and do not alone establish causal effects on crime."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":31,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"Homicide deaths fell 17.3% from the 2018 comparison point to the end-period comparison, and reported crime per 100,000 inhabitants fell 12% from 2018 to 2023; robbery, extortion, vehicle theft, and household robbery also declined. At the same time, other crimes against personal liberty rose 59.5%, other crimes against life rose 104.5%, lesions rose 35.8%, and reported crime increased 15.9% from 2022 to 2023. The report notes doubts about homicide measurement because homicide declines coincided with increases in other lethal and liberty-related offenses.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.9","5B.7","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The outcome comparison includes 2023 and the 2022-2023 change.","ruler_attribution":"The trends are assessed in relation to AMLO's security policy, but the source identifies alternative explanations and measurement uncertainty.","limitations":["The report cautions that official homicide reductions may reflect undercounting or classification changes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":38,"end_unit":44,"fact_summary":"From 2018 to 2023, justice-system personnel fell 8%, FGR spending fell 28.4%, and administrative units fell 22.6%; pending investigations rose 60.3%. Illegal detentions remained above 20% at the state level and 11% federally on average, prison occupancy rose above capacity, and prison complaints increased 866.4%. Impunity remained above 90%, feminicide impunity rose 8.8 percentage points from 2021 to 2023, and the criminal-justice rule-of-law factor declined 5.2% from 2018 to 2024.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","4B.4","5B.7","6B.5","6B.8","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The institutional and outcome data include 2023; one rule-of-law measure extends to 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the deterioration to the administration's justice and security management.","limitations":["Some aggregate indicators cover multiple institutions and cannot isolate presidential control from state-level responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":52,"end_unit":55,"fact_summary":"The report's subnational QCA found that homicide reduction in 2019-2023 was not consistently associated with greater GN activity; reductions occurred even where all GN factors were absent, and some states with greater GN presence experienced increased homicide. In controlled comparisons, absence of GN operations was the sole minimized configuration associated with homicide reduction, with 100% coverage and consistency in that solution. The report concludes that GN activity was not determinative of state-level homicide reductions.","question_ids":["3B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The analysis directly covers 2019-2023, including the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The finding evaluates the federal GN strategy associated with AMLO.","limitations":["This is a qualitative comparative analysis of 32 subnational cases; it does not prove that GN operations increased violence in every location."]},{"source_id":"SRC-accb4d26e6454348","start_unit":56,"end_unit":57,"fact_summary":"The report's overall balance is clearly negative despite some positive results: AMLO allegedly left a more violent and equally impune country, fewer institutional capacities, expanded criminal regimes, and permanent militarization. It also identifies positive results including GN infrastructure, reductions in several urban crimes and insecurity perceptions, lower crime costs, and increased public confidence in armed forces and local police.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.10","4B.10","5B.10","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The balance summarizes the administration through the end of the six-year period, with several metrics ending in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment is explicitly about López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["The report's overall judgment is an interpretation, not a score or official finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The IMF reported broad-based 2023 expansion, projected real GDP growth of 3.2%, unemployment of 2.7%, declining inflation, and resilient banking. It credited very strong policies and policy frameworks with restraining public debt and containing inflation, while noting that sustainable and inclusive growth required structural reforms.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The evidence directly concerns Mexico's 2023 economic performance under AMLO.","ruler_attribution":"The IMF assesses policies of the Mexican authorities during AMLO's presidency; it does not attribute every outcome personally to López Obrador.","limitations":["The IMF assessment is country-level and does not establish individual presidential causation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The IMF recommended maintaining sustainable fiscal policy while increasing infrastructure, education, and social support; strengthening the fiscal framework; enhancing regulatory-agency autonomy and AML/CFT implementation; and pursuing reforms for female labor participation, crime, corruption, finance, competition, renewable energy, and formalization.","question_ids":["5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","8B.1","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"These are recommendations made during the 2023 Article IV review, identifying policy gaps relevant to the period.","ruler_attribution":"Recommendations concern the Mexican authorities rather than solely AMLO.","limitations":["Recommendations show identified needs, not necessarily that AMLO rejected or failed to implement each one."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The IMF judged the proposed 2024 budget procyclical, with a 2.4% of GDP fiscal impulse and a projected 5.4% deficit while the economy was above potential and inflation remained above target. It warned that achieving the planned 2025 consolidation would require additional measures, and called for higher non-oil revenue, better-targeted social protection, more efficient education spending, and stronger fiscal transparency.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.5","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The budget was proposed in 2023 by the outgoing AMLO administration, making the warning directly relevant to the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The IMF attributes the budget proposal to the Mexican authorities under AMLO.","limitations":["The main fiscal effects were projected for 2024 and therefore are not fully observed in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"The IMF found Mexico well positioned for nearshoring but noted that announced investment had not yet produced clear aggregate macroeconomic effects. It reported that authorities had a broad supply-side agenda involving infrastructure, trade, minimum wages, labor law, female participation, crime and corruption, finance, formalization, and energy, while warning that regulatory and supply-side constraints remained.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","5B.8","5B.10","6B.3","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment is based on developments through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The agenda is attributed to Mexican authorities during AMLO's administration.","limitations":["The source does not establish which agenda items were enacted or implemented by López Obrador personally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":25,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"Mexico's minimum wage rose 80% in real terms since 2018; the IMF said early increases likely raised low-income wages but warned later increases could increase informality or reduce job creation. The authorities said their wage, trade, infrastructure, and labor policies promoted equitable growth and formal jobs, while acknowledging remaining gender and childcare gaps.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.3","6B.8","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence compares policy since 2018 and evaluates conditions relevant in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The wage and labor-policy positions are attributed to the AMLO authorities; the adverse employment risk is the IMF's assessment.","limitations":["The source does not provide 2023 distributional outcomes by region, gender, or group."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":35,"end_unit":36,"fact_summary":"The IMF found Mexico's financial system resilient, with high capital and liquidity buffers, but identified outstanding AML/CFT gaps, weak beneficial-ownership controls, incomplete supervision of non-financial businesses and professions, and insufficient agency autonomy and resources. Authorities reported some cyber-response, liquidity-testing, and resolution-planning improvements, while several FSAP recommendations had no measures taken.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.9","5B.3","5B.5","5B.7","7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence covers the 2023 financial-sector review and reported implementation status during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The IMF evaluates Mexican authorities and regulators during AMLO's administration; many functions were institutionally assigned to autonomous or specialized bodies.","limitations":["The source does not establish direct presidential interference with regulators."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":46,"end_unit":49,"fact_summary":"Mexico increased its 2030 emissions-reduction target from 22% to 30% and had a climate strategy covering energy, transport, waste, land use, agriculture, and industry. It had a carbon tax, a pilot emissions-trading system, green-finance and green-bond initiatives, and plans for electric vehicles and deforestation control, but the IMF found the carbon price modest and warned that continued Pemex investment risked stranded assets.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.9","1B.10","5B.1","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The target revision and policy status were reported in the 2023 Article IV consultation.","ruler_attribution":"The climate commitments and energy policies are attributed to Mexican authorities under AMLO.","limitations":["The source evaluates national climate policy and does not measure actual 2023 emissions outcomes against the target."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":53,"end_unit":55,"fact_summary":"The FSAP implementation table reported no measures taken on regulatory-agency autonomy, organizational resources, consolidated supervision, and refinement of risk-based supervision. It reported ongoing or partial work on liquidity stress tests, macroprudential strategy, cybersecurity, climate-risk guidance, open banking, and a sustainable taxonomy.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.9","5B.3","5B.5","5B.7","7B.6","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The status table reports implementation during the 2023 review.","ruler_attribution":"The actions and omissions are attributed to Mexican authorities and regulators, not exclusively to AMLO.","limitations":["Some reforms fall within autonomous agencies' mandates and cannot be attributed solely to the president."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":88,"end_unit":92,"fact_summary":"The IMF found corruption among Mexico's highest money-laundering risks and reported that the anti-corruption system had legal and institutional foundations, but high-level corruption prosecutions were absent, enforcement was inadequate, beneficial-ownership information unreliable, and non-financial gatekeepers lacked required PEP due-diligence obligations. The IMF recommended stronger coordination, resources, sanctions, asset recovery, and verification of beneficial ownership in procurement.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings concern the institutional and enforcement status reviewed in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates Mexico's anti-corruption institutions and authorities during AMLO's administration; it does not establish personal enrichment by López Obrador.","limitations":["The evidence does not prove that AMLO personally directed corruption or benefited from it."]},{"source_id":"SRC-684988a395d1a128","start_unit":103,"end_unit":105,"fact_summary":"The IMF found limited foreign-bribery risk but reported no completed foreign-bribery prosecution, inadequate whistleblower protection, unclear corporate liability, and unresolved deficiencies in PEP monitoring, beneficial-ownership identification, suspicious-transaction reporting, and DNFBP supervision. It acknowledged legal and institutional reforms and broader PEP controls while calling for effective enforcement.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The supplementary information updates the assessment as of October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Mexican authorities and institutions under AMLO; they do not establish personal conduct by López Obrador.","limitations":["The source explicitly notes that some information supplied by Mexico was not independently verified by the OECD monitoring body."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The sources are broad country-level and policy evaluations; many facts concern institutional outcomes or subnational authorities rather than actions personally ordered by López Obrador.","Some supplied documents and facts extend beyond calendar 2023 to assess the full 2018-2024 administration; those extensions are identified in the relevant period_fit or limitations fields.","No facts are scored."]}
